audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Pilate/Herod trials, Barabbas, daughters of Jerusalem, crucifixion, forgiveness textual variant, criminals, death, centurion, women witnesses, Joseph burial.

verses.restored: The whole multitude of them rose and led him to Pilate.

familiar.text: And the whole multitude of them arose, and led him unto Pilate.

modern.text: Then the whole council rose and led Jesus away to Pilate.

original.text: Καὶ ἀναστὰν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Πιλᾶτον.

verses.restored: They began to accuse him, saying, We found this one misleading our nation, forbidding tribute to Caesar, and saying he himself is Messiah, a king.

familiar.text: And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this fellow perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ a King.

modern.text: And they began to accuse Him, saying, “We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding payment of taxes to Caesar, and proclaiming Himself to be Christ, a King.”

original.text: ἤρξαντο δὲ κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Τοῦτον εὕραμεν διαστρέφοντα τὸ ἔθνος ⸀ἡμῶν καὶ κωλύοντα ⸂φόρους Καίσαρι⸃ διδόναι ⸀καὶ λέγοντα ⸀αὑτὸν χριστὸν βασιλέα εἶναι.

verses.restored: Pilate questioned him, saying, Are you the king of the Judeans? Answering him, he said, You say it.

familiar.text: And Pilate asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answered him and said, Thou sayest it.

modern.text: So Pilate asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ⸀ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.

verses.restored: Pilate said to the chief priests and crowds, I find no cause in this human.

familiar.text: Then said Pilate to the chief priests and to the people, I find no fault in this man.

modern.text: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους· Οὐδὲν εὑρίσκω αἴτιον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ.

verses.restored: But they were insisting, saying, He stirs up the people, teaching through all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to here.

familiar.text: And they were the more fierce, saying, He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry, beginning from Galilee to this place.

modern.text: But they kept insisting, “He stirs up the people all over Judea with His teaching. He began in Galilee and has come all the way here.” Jesus before Herod

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἐπίσχυον λέγοντες ὅτι Ἀνασείει τὸν λαὸν διδάσκων καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ⸀καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἕως ὧδε.

verses.restored: Pilate, hearing this, asked whether the person was Galilean.

familiar.text: When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man were a Galilaean.

modern.text: When Pilate heard this, he asked if the man was a Galilean.

original.text: Πιλᾶτος δὲ ⸀ἀκούσας ἐπηρώτησεν εἰ ὁ ἄνθρωπος Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν,

verses.restored: Learning that he was from Herod's authority, he sent him up to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem in those days.

familiar.text: And as soon as he knew that he belonged unto Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem at that time.

modern.text: And learning that Jesus was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, who himself was in Jerusalem at that time.

original.text: καὶ ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου ἐστὶν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν πρὸς Ἡρῴδην, ὄντα καὶ αὐτὸν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις.

verses.restored: Herod, seeing Jesus, rejoiced greatly, for he had long wanted to see him because of hearing about him, and he hoped to see some sign happen through him.

familiar.text: And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he was desirous to see him of a long season, because he had heard many things of him; and he hoped to have seen some miracle done by him.

modern.text: When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased. He had wanted to see Him for a long time, because he had heard about Him and was hoping to see Him perform a miracle.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐχάρη λίαν, ἦν γὰρ ⸂ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων θέλων⸃ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ ⸀ἀκούειν περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤλπιζέν τι σημεῖον ἰδεῖν ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ γινόμενον.

verses.restored: He questioned him with many words, but Jesus answered him nothing.

familiar.text: Then he questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing.

modern.text: Herod questioned Jesus at great length, but He gave no answer.

original.text: ἐπηρώτα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν λόγοις ἱκανοῖς· αὐτὸς δὲ οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: The chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing him.

familiar.text: And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused him.

modern.text: Meanwhile, the chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing Him.

original.text: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς εὐτόνως κατηγοροῦντες αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Herod with his soldiers treated him as nothing, mocked him, clothed him in bright clothing, and sent him back to Pilate.

familiar.text: And Herod with his men of war set him at nought, and mocked him, and arrayed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him again to Pilate.

modern.text: And even Herod and his soldiers ridiculed and mocked Him. Dressing Him in a fine robe, they sent Him back to Pilate.

original.text: ἐξουθενήσας δὲ αὐτὸν ⸀καὶ ὁ Ἡρῴδης σὺν τοῖς στρατεύμασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμπαίξας ⸀περιβαλὼν ἐσθῆτα λαμπρὰν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν τῷ Πιλάτῳ.

verses.restored: Herod and Pilate became friends with one another that day; before this they had been in hostility with each other.

familiar.text: And the same day Pilate and Herod were made friends together: for before they were at enmity between themselves.

modern.text: That day Herod and Pilate became friends; before this time they had been enemies. The Crowd Chooses Barabbas (Matthew 27:15–23; Mark 15:6–11)

original.text: ἐγένοντο δὲ φίλοι ὅ τε ⸂Ἡρῴδης καὶ ὁ Πιλᾶτος⸃ ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μετʼ ἀλλήλων· προϋπῆρχον γὰρ ἐν ἔχθρᾳ ὄντες πρὸς ⸀αὑτούς.

verses.restored: Pilate called together the chief priests, rulers, and people,

familiar.text: And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,

modern.text: Then Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,

original.text: Πιλᾶτος δὲ συγκαλεσάμενος τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τὸν λαὸν

verses.restored: and said to them, You brought me this person as one turning the people away. Look, having examined him before you, I found in this person no cause for the charges you bring against him.

familiar.text: Said unto them, Ye have brought this man unto me, as one that perverteth the people: and, behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him:

modern.text: and said to them, “You brought me this man as one who was inciting the people to rebellion. I have examined Him here in your presence and found Him not guilty of your charges against Him.

original.text: εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Προσηνέγκατέ μοι τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὡς ἀποστρέφοντα τὸν λαόν, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ἀνακρίνας ⸀οὐθὲν εὗρον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ αἴτιον ὧν κατηγορεῖτε κατʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Neither did Herod, for he sent him back to us. Look, nothing worthy of death has been done by him.

familiar.text: No, nor yet Herod: for I sent you to him; and, lo, nothing worthy of death is done unto him.

modern.text: Neither has Herod, for he sent Him back to us. As you can see, He has done nothing deserving of death.

original.text: ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ Ἡρῴδης, ⸂ἀνέπεμψεν γὰρ αὐτὸν πρὸς ἡμᾶς⸃· καὶ ἰδοὺ οὐδὲν ἄξιον θανάτου ἐστὶν πεπραγμένον αὐτῷ·

verses.restored: Therefore, after disciplining him, I will release him.

familiar.text: I will therefore chastise him, and release him.

modern.text: Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.”

original.text: παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ⸀ἀπολύσω.

verses.restored: [Some later manuscripts add that he had obligation to release one to them at the feast.]

familiar.text: (For of necessity he must release one unto them at the feast.)

modern.note: The BSB follows modern critical-text practice here and does not print this traditional verse number as a separate verse.

original.note: This traditional verse number is not present as a separate verse in the SBLGNT base text; preserve as a textual-witness issue.

verses.restored: But they cried out all together, saying, Take this one away, and release Barabbas to us.

familiar.text: And they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas:

modern.text: But they all cried out in unison: “Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!”

original.text: ⸀Ἀνέκραγον δὲ παμπληθεὶ λέγοντες· Αἶρε τοῦτον, ἀπόλυσον δὲ ἡμῖν ⸀τὸν Βαραββᾶν·

verses.restored: He had been thrown into prison because of an uprising in the city and murder.

familiar.text: (Who for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.)

modern.text: (Barabbas had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder.)

original.text: ὅστις ἦν διὰ στάσιν τινὰ γενομένην ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ φόνον ⸂βληθεὶς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ⸃.

verses.restored: Pilate addressed them again, wanting to release Jesus.

familiar.text: Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spake again to them.

modern.text: Wanting to release Jesus, Pilate addressed them again,

original.text: πάλιν ⸀δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ⸀προσεφώνησεν, θέλων ἀπολῦσαι τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

verses.restored: But they kept shouting, Crucify, crucify him.

familiar.text: But they cried, saying, Crucify him, crucify him.

modern.text: but they kept shouting, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἐπεφώνουν λέγοντες· ⸂Σταύρου σταύρου⸃ αὐτόν.

verses.restored: A third time he said to them, Why, what harm did this one do? I found no cause of death in him. Therefore, after disciplining him, I will release him.

familiar.text: And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him, and let him go.

modern.text: A third time he said to them, “What evil has this man done? I have found in Him no offense worthy of death. So after I punish Him, I will release Him.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ τρίτον εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν οὗτος; οὐδὲν αἴτιον θανάτου εὗρον ἐν αὐτῷ· παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω.

verses.restored: But they pressed with loud voices, asking that he be crucified, and their voices prevailed.

familiar.text: And they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. And the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed.

modern.text: But they were insistent, demanding with loud voices for Jesus to be crucified. And their clamor prevailed.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἐπέκειντο φωναῖς μεγάλαις αἰτούμενοι αὐτὸν σταυρωθῆναι, καὶ κατίσχυον αἱ φωναὶ ⸀αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: Pilate decided that their demand should happen.

familiar.text: And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.

modern.text: So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met.

original.text: ⸀καὶ Πιλᾶτος ἐπέκρινεν γενέσθαι τὸ αἴτημα αὐτῶν·

verses.restored: He released the one thrown into prison for uprising and murder, whom they asked for, but Jesus he handed over to their will.

familiar.text: And he released unto them him that for sedition and murder was cast into prison, whom they had desired; but he delivered Jesus to their will.

modern.text: As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder, and handed Jesus over to their will. The Crucifixion (Psalms 22:1–31; Matthew 27:32–44; Mark 15:21–32; John 19:16–27)

original.text: ἀπέλυσεν δὲ τὸν διὰ στάσιν καὶ φόνον βεβλημένον ⸀εἰς φυλακὴν ὃν ᾐτοῦντο, τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν παρέδωκεν τῷ θελήματι αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: As they led him away, taking hold of Simon of Cyrene coming from the country, they laid the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.

familiar.text: And as they led him away, they laid hold upon one Simon, a Cyrenian, coming out of the country, and on him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus.

modern.text: As the soldiers led Him away, they seized Simon of Cyrene on his way in from the country, and put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.

original.text: Καὶ ὡς ἀπήγαγον αὐτόν, ἐπιλαβόμενοι ⸂Σίμωνά τινα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον⸃ ἀπʼ ἀγροῦ ἐπέθηκαν αὐτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν φέρειν ὄπισθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: A great multitude of the people and women followed him, mourning and lamenting for him.

familiar.text: And there followed him a great company of people, and of women, which also bewailed and lamented him.

modern.text: A great number of people followed Him, including women who kept mourning and wailing for Him.

original.text: Ἠκολούθει δὲ αὐτῷ πολὺ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ γυναικῶν ⸀αἳ ἐκόπτοντο καὶ ἐθρήνουν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Turning to them, Jesus said, Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me; rather weep for yourselves and for your children.

familiar.text: But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.

modern.text: But Jesus turned to them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.

original.text: στραφεὶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὰς ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ, μὴ κλαίετε ἐπʼ ἐμέ· πλὴν ἐφʼ ἑαυτὰς κλαίετε καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν,

verses.restored: For look, days are coming in which they will say, Blessed are the barren, the wombs that did not bear, and breasts that did not nurse.

familiar.text: For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.

modern.text: Look, the days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that never bore, and breasts that never nursed!’

original.text: ὅτι ἰδοὺ ἔρχονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς ἐροῦσιν Μακάριαι αἱ στεῖραι καὶ ⸀αἱ κοιλίαι αἳ οὐκ ἐγέννησαν καὶ μαστοὶ οἳ οὐκ ⸀ἔθρεψαν.

verses.restored: Then they will begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us, and to the hills, Cover us.

familiar.text: Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.

modern.text: At that time ‘they will say to the mountains, “Fall on us!” and to the hills, “Cover us!”’

original.text: τότε ἄρξονται λέγειν τοῖς ὄρεσιν· Πέσετε ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς, καὶ τοῖς βουνοῖς· Καλύψατε ἡμᾶς·

verses.restored: For if they do these things when the wood is green, what will happen when it is dry?

familiar.text: For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

modern.text: For if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?”

original.text: ὅτι εἰ ἐν ⸀τῷ ὑγρῷ ξύλῳ ταῦτα ποιοῦσιν, ἐν τῷ ξηρῷ τί γένηται;

verses.restored: Two others also, criminals, were led with him to be executed.

familiar.text: And there were also two other, malefactors, led with him to be put to death.

modern.text: Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.

original.text: Ἤγοντο δὲ καὶ ἕτεροι ⸂κακοῦργοι δύο⸃ σὺν αὐτῷ ἀναιρεθῆναι.

verses.restored: When they came to the place called Skull, there they crucified him and the criminals, one at his right and one at his left.

familiar.text: And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.

modern.text: When they came to the place called The Skull, they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.

original.text: καὶ ὅτε ⸀ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Κρανίον, ἐκεῖ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς κακούργους, ὃν μὲν ἐκ δεξιῶν ὃν δὲ ἐξ ἀριστερῶν.

verses.restored: [Jesus said, Father, release them, for they do not know what they are doing.] They divided his garments, casting lots.

familiar.text: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.

modern.text: Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided up His garments by casting lots.

original.text: ⸂ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν· Πάτερ, ἄφες αὐτοῖς, οὐ γὰρ οἴδασιν τί ποιοῦσιν.⸃ διαμεριζόμενοι δὲ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἔβαλον ⸀κλήρους.

verses.restored: The people stood watching. The rulers were sneering, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if this is the Messiah of the Divine, the Chosen One.

familiar.text: And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also with them derided him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he be Christ, the chosen of God.

modern.text: The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”

original.text: καὶ εἱστήκει ὁ λαὸς θεωρῶν. ἐξεμυκτήριζον δὲ καὶ οἱ ⸀ἄρχοντες λέγοντες· Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, σωσάτω ἑαυτόν, εἰ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστὸς ⸂τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ⸃ ἐκλεκτός.

verses.restored: The soldiers also mocked him, coming near and offering sour wine,

familiar.text: And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, and offering him vinegar,

modern.text: The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine.

original.text: ⸀ἐνέπαιξαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται προσερχόμενοι, ⸀ὄξος προσφέροντες αὐτῷ

verses.restored: and saying, If you are the king of the Judeans, save yourself.

familiar.text: And saying, If thou be the king of the Jews, save thyself.

modern.text: “If You are the King of the Jews,” they said, “save Yourself!”

original.text: καὶ λέγοντες· Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων, σῶσον σεαυτόν.

verses.restored: There was also an inscription over him: This is the king of the Judeans.

familiar.text: And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

modern.text: Above Him was posted an inscription: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

original.text: ἦν δὲ καὶ ⸀ἐπιγραφὴ ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτῷ· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων ⸀οὗτος.

verses.restored: One of the criminals hanging there blasphemed him, saying, Are you not the Messiah? Save yourself and us.

familiar.text: And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.

modern.text: One of the criminals who hung there heaped abuse on Him. “Are You not the Christ?” he said. “Save Yourself and us!”

original.text: Εἷς δὲ τῶν κρεμασθέντων κακούργων ἐβλασφήμει αὐτόν ⸀λέγων· ⸀Οὐχὶ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός; σῶσον σεαυτὸν καὶ ἡμᾶς.

verses.restored: But the other answered, rebuking him, saying, Do you not even fear the Divine, since you are under the same judgment?

familiar.text: But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?

modern.text: But the other one rebuked him, saying, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἕτερος ⸂ἐπιτιμῶν αὐτῷ ἔφη⸃· Οὐδὲ φοβῇ σὺ τὸν θεόν, ὅτι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ κρίματι εἶ;

verses.restored: We indeed justly, for we receive what is worthy of what we did; but this one did nothing out of place.

familiar.text: And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.

modern.text: We are punished justly, for we are receiving what our actions deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.”

original.text: καὶ ἡμεῖς μὲν δικαίως, ἄξια γὰρ ὧν ἐπράξαμεν ἀπολαμβάνομεν· οὗτος δὲ οὐδὲν ἄτοπον ἔπραξεν.

verses.restored: He said, Jesus, remember me when you come into your reign.

familiar.text: And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.

modern.text: Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!”

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἔλεγεν· Ἰησοῦ, μνήσθητί ⸀μου ὅταν ἔλθῃς ⸂ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ⸃ σου.

verses.restored: He said to him, Amen, I say to you: today you will be with me in Paradise.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

modern.text: And Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.” The Death of Jesus (Psalms 31:1–24; Matthew 27:45–56; Mark 15:33–41; John 19:28–30)

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν ⸀αὐτῷ· Ἀμήν ⸂σοι λέγω⸃ σήμερον μετʼ ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ.

verses.restored: It was already about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,

familiar.text: And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.

modern.text: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.

original.text: ⸂Καὶ ἦν⸃ ⸀ἤδη ὡσεὶ ὥρα ἕκτη καὶ σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης

verses.restored: the sun failing; and the curtain of the temple was torn in the middle.

familiar.text: And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.

modern.text: The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.

original.text: ⸂τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος⸃, ἐσχίσθη ⸀δὲ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ μέσον.

verses.restored: Calling out with a great voice, Jesus said, Father, into your hands I entrust my spirit. Saying this, he breathed out.

familiar.text: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.

modern.text: Then Jesus called out in a loud voice, “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.” And when He had said this, He breathed His last.

original.text: καὶ φωνήσας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πάτερ, εἰς χεῖράς σου ⸀παρατίθεμαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου. ⸂τοῦτο δὲ⸃ εἰπὼν ἐξέπνευσεν.

verses.restored: When the centurion saw what happened, he glorified the Divine, saying, Truly this human was righteous.

familiar.text: Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.

modern.text: When the centurion saw what had happened, he gave glory to God, saying, “Surely this was a righteous man. ”

original.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης τὸ γενόμενον ⸀ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεὸν λέγων· Ὄντως ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος ἦν.

verses.restored: All the crowds that had gathered for this spectacle, seeing the things that happened, returned beating their chests.

familiar.text: And all the people that came together to that sight, beholding the things which were done, smote their breasts, and returned.

modern.text: And when all the people who had gathered for this spectacle saw what had happened, they returned home beating their breasts.

original.text: καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαραγενόμενοι ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τὴν θεωρίαν ταύτην, ⸀θεωρήσαντες τὰ γενόμενα, ⸀τύπτοντες τὰ στήθη ὑπέστρεφον.

verses.restored: All those who knew him stood far away, and the women who followed him from Galilee, seeing these things.

familiar.text: And all his acquaintance, and the women that followed him from Galilee, stood afar off, beholding these things.

modern.text: But all those who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed Him from Galilee, stood at a distance watching these things. The Burial of Jesus (Isaiah 53:9–12; Matthew 27:57–61; Mark 15:42–47; John 19:38–42)

original.text: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ πάντες οἱ γνωστοὶ ⸀αὐτῷ ⸀μακρόθεν, καὶ γυναῖκες αἱ ⸀συνακολουθοῦσαι αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὁρῶσαι ταῦτα.

verses.restored: Look, a man named Joseph, a council member, a good and righteous man,

familiar.text: And, behold, there was a man named Joseph, a counsellor; and he was a good man, and a just:

modern.text: Now there was a Council member named Joseph, a good and righteous man,

original.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Ἰωσὴφ βουλευτὴς ὑπάρχων, ⸀ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ δίκαιος—

verses.restored: who had not consented to their counsel and action, from Arimathea, a city of the Judeans, who was waiting for the reign of the Divine;

familiar.text: (The same had not consented to the counsel and deed of them;) he was of Arimathaea, a city of the Jews: who also himself waited for the kingdom of God.

modern.text: who had not consented to their decision or action. He was from the Judean town of Arimathea, and was waiting for the kingdom of God.

original.text: οὗτος οὐκ ἦν συγκατατεθειμένος τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν— ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας πόλεως τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὃς ⸀προσεδέχετο τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ,

verses.restored: this one came to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

familiar.text: This man went unto Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus.

modern.text: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.

original.text: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ,

verses.restored: Taking it down, he wrapped it in linen and placed him in a tomb cut in stone, where no one had yet been laid.

familiar.text: And he took it down, and wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a sepulchre that was hewn in stone, wherein never man before was laid.

modern.text: Then he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and placed it in a tomb cut into the rock, where no one had yet been laid.

original.text: καὶ ⸀καθελὼν ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι, καὶ ἔθηκεν ⸀αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ οὗ οὐκ ἦν ⸂οὐδεὶς οὔπω⸃ κείμενος.

verses.restored: It was Preparation day, and Sabbath was dawning.

familiar.text: And that day was the preparation, and the sabbath drew on.

modern.text: It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was beginning.

original.text: καὶ ἡμέρα ἦν ⸂παρασκευῆς, καὶ⸃ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκεν.

verses.restored: The women who had come with him from Galilee followed and saw the tomb and how his body was placed.

familiar.text: And the women also, which came with him from Galilee, followed after, and beheld the sepulchre, and how his body was laid.

modern.text: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed, and they saw the tomb and how His body was placed.

original.text: κατακολουθήσασαι δὲ ⸀αἱ γυναῖκες, αἵτινες ἦσαν συνεληλυθυῖαι ⸂ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας αὐτῷ⸃, ἐθεάσαντο τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ ὡς ἐτέθη τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: Returning, they prepared spices and ointments. On the Sabbath they rested according to the command.

familiar.text: And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment.

modern.text: Then they returned to prepare spices and perfumes. And they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment.

original.text: ὑποστρέψασαι δὲ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα. Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν,
